sentences.text:
The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined insurance company of Tata Sumo - original opponent No.3, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 07.02.103 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Panchmahals at Godhra in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1256 of 2006, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.8,03,000/- with 9% per annum interest from the date of filing claim petition/s till its realization, to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No.1 to 3 i.e. driver,
owner and insurance company of the Tata Sumo Car bearing registration No.GJ-17-C-7407 liable,
jointly and several.
It is noted that opponents No.4 to 6 i.e. driver, owner and insurance company of Rickshaw bearing registration No.GJ-6-Y-1842 are exonerated by the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts of the case, as per claimant/s, are as under :
2.1

That on 05.08.2006 at about 20:00 hours, deceased - Premilaben Arvindbhai Rathwa was travelling in the Rickshaw bearing registration No.GJ-6-Y-1842 driven by opponent No.4 and was going from Halol to Pavagadh.

When they were passing through Khudpir village, at that time, opponent No.1 came driving the Tata Sumo Car bearing registration No.GJ-17-C-7407 in rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed heavily with the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined rickshaw.
As a result, the deceased sustained serious injuries and ultimately, deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased - husband and three minor children have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.7.50 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 & 2 and 4 & 5 i.e. driver and owner of the Tata Sumo and Rickshaw, respectively, have appeared but not filed written statement contesting the claim petition.

Opponent No.3 & 6 i.e. insurance companies of the Tata Sumo Car and Rickshaw have appeared and filed their written statements / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimants in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.

After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly United India Insurance Company Limited vs Bipinkumar Manilal Mardiya on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158802532/
2 allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

sentences.text: 2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the appellant - insurance company for exoneration.

3. Learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati for the appellant - insurance company of the Tata Sumo Car (original opponent No.3) has mainly raised contention before this Court that while awarding loss of dependency benefits, the Tribunal has deducted 1/10 th amount for personal expenses of the deceased, which should be 1/4 th looking to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the Tribunal has exceeded its jurisdiction, as the claimants have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.7.5 lakhs, whereas the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.8,03,000/-, which is more than the prayer by the claimants.
He has submitted that the award may be modified and this appeal may be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Hiren Modi for respondent No.6, 8 and 9 - original claimants has faily submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly deducted 1/10 th amount for personal expenses, which should be 1/4 th as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

He has also fairly NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly considered the prospective income of 50%, which should be 40% as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
However, he has submitted that the Tribunal has not properly considered multiplier while awarding compensation, which should be 18, instead of 17.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of the deceased.
He has also submitted that the Tribunal has not properly considered the general and non-conventional damages as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

In support of his submissions, he has relied upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of (i) Pranay Shethi (supra) (ii) Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (iii) Magma General Insurance Company Limited versus Nanu Ram and Others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and (iv) United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780.

5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be United India Insurance Company Limited vs Bipinkumar Manilal Mardiya on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158802532/
3 determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

sentences.text: It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6.1 Keeping in mind the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the Tribunal has wrongly calculated 1/10 th amount for personal deduction and 17 multiplier while awarding compensation of loss of dependency benefits; and that the Tribunal has not properly considered the general and non-pecuniary damages while awarding compensation.

If we calculate the award impugned, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), Sarla NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined Verma (supra), Magma (supra) and Satinder (supra), the total compensation would be little more than the award, as the multiplier would 18 and general and non-pecuniary damages would be increased.
However, since there is no cross-appeal/cross-objection by the claimants, it would not be proper to enhance the award.

6.2 Under the circumstances, this Court finds that the impugned award, at the hands of the appellant - insurance company of the Tata Sumo - original opponent No.3, is just and proper and this Court does not warrant any interference in it.
8. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is hereby dismissed.

8.2 The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire awarded amount, if yet not deposited, with interest and cost as decided by the Tribunal, from the date of claim petition till its realisation, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2858/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 8.3

The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal (including enhanced amount), with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the respective claimant/s, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the court fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) M.H. DAVE United India Insurance Company Limited vs Bipinkumar Manilal Mardiya on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158802532/
